steps.title: Import Vue and defineTestSetup from @vue/test-utils
steps.instruction: Import Vue and defineTestSetup from the @vue/test-utils package to prepare for component testing.
steps.hint: Use named imports from '@vue/test-utils' to bring in Vue and defineTestSetup.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing from a package
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The testing utilities are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: Vue and defineTestSetup are imported from '@vue/test-utils'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the necessary testing utilities.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Vue and defineTestSetup from '@vue/test-utils'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're importing Vue and defineTestSetup from the correct package '@vue/test-utils'.

steps.title: Create a basic Vue component for testing
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'TestComponent' that returns a template with a heading and a paragraph displaying a reactive message.
steps.hint:
Define a component with a template that includes an

and a

element. Use the options API with a data function that returns an object containing a message property.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue and defineTestSetup from '@vue/test-utils'

// Create a Vue component named 'TestComponent' here
steps.expectedOutcome:
A Vue component named TestComponent is defined with a template containing an

and a

element that displays a reactive message.
successCriteria: TestComponent is defined as a Vue component with a template and a data function returning an object with a message property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a basic Vue component that will serve as our test subject.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the component, but make sure it has both a template with the required elements and a data function returning a message property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component definition is missing or incomplete. Create a Vue component named TestComponent with a template and reactive data.

steps.title: Initialize component data with reactive properties
steps.instruction: Inside the TestComponent, add a data function that returns an object with a property 'message' set to 'Hello from Vue!'
steps.hint: In Vue components, the data option should be a function that returns an object containing reactive properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TestComponent now has reactive data initialized with a 'message' property.
successCriteria: TestComponent has a data function that returns an object containing a 'message' property set to 'Hello from Vue!'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added reactive data to your Vue component. This 'message' property can now be used in the template and tested.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your data function returns an object with exactly the 'message' property set to 'Hello from Vue!'
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't have the required data function. Remember to add a data function that returns an object with a 'message' property.

steps.title: Create a computed property for testing
steps.instruction: Inside your component, add a computed property named 'message' that returns a string combining the component's data properties.
steps.hint: In Vue, computed properties are defined in the 'computed' option. Create a function that returns a string using the data properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a computed property that depends on its data, making it reactive to changes.
successCriteria: A computed property named 'message' is defined in the component's computed option.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a computed property that will react to changes in the component's data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the computed property is properly defined in the 'computed' option and returns a value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The computed property is missing or incorrectly defined. Check that it's in the 'computed' option and returns a value based on data properties.

steps.title: Add a method to modify component state
steps.instruction: In your component, add a 'methods' object with a method called 'incrementCounter' that increases a 'counter' data property by 1 when called.
steps.hint: Add a 'methods' property to your component object, then define a method inside it that accesses 'this.counter' and increments it.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component now has a method that can modify its reactive state, which will be useful for testing state changes.
successCriteria: The component has a 'methods' object containing an 'incrementCounter' method that increments 'this.counter' by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a method that modifies component state. This is essential for testing state changes in Vue components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your method is properly defined in the 'methods' object and actually increments the counter value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method isn't correctly implemented. Check that you've added a 'methods' object with an 'incrementCounter' method that increases 'this.counter'.

steps.title: Set up the test context using defineTestSetup
steps.instruction: Call defineTestSetup to create a test context for your component, passing the component as the first argument.
steps.hint: Use defineTestSetup with your component as the argument. This sets up the testing environment.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a test context
const testContext = defineTestSetup(MyComponent);
steps.expectedOutcome: A test context is created using defineTestSetup, ready for writing tests.
successCriteria: defineTestSetup is called with the component as an argument.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully set up the test context using defineTestSetup.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling defineTestSetup with your component as the argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test context isn't set up correctly. Use defineTestSetup with your component.

steps.title: Write a test to check initial component state
steps.instruction: Inside the defineTestSetup call, write a test that verifies the component's counter data property has an initial value of 0.
steps.hint: Use the test function to write a test case that checks if the component's data.counter equals 0.
steps.expectedOutcome: A test is added to verify that the component's counter data property starts at 0.
successCriteria: The test function is defined inside tests and checks that component.data().counter equals 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully written a test to verify the initial state of the component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your test specifically checks that component.data().counter equals 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test doesn't correctly verify the initial counter value. Check the example and try again.

steps.title: Test computed property values in the context
steps.instruction: In the defineTestSetup configuration, add a second test that checks the computed property returns the expected value based on component data.
steps.hint: Add another test case inside the tests function that accesses the computed property and asserts its value matches expectations.
steps.expectedOutcome: The test suite will now include a test that verifies the computed property's value based on component data.
successCriteria: A second test case is added inside the tests function that checks the computed property value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a test for the computed property. This ensures your computed properties work correctly within the test context.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a test, but make sure it specifically checks the computed property value. Look at the analogous example for the correct structure.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test for the computed property is missing or incorrect. Review how to write test cases in Vue Test Utils and try again.

steps.title: Test component method execution and state changes
steps.instruction: Inside the tests function, add a test that calls the incrementCounter method and verifies the counter data property increases.
steps.hint: Use the component instance from the test context to call the method and check the updated data value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A test case that verifies the incrementCounter method correctly updates the counter data property.
successCriteria: The test calls incrementCounter on the component instance and asserts that counter equals 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully tested a component method that modifies reactive state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your test calls the incrementCounter method and checks the updated counter value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test should call the incrementCounter method and verify the counter data property increases to 1.

steps.title: Test component with different props in context
steps.instruction: Add a new test case inside the tests function that passes a prop to the component and verifies the component's behavior changes accordingly.
steps.hint: Use wrapper.setProps() to pass props to the component within the test context, then check if the component's state or computed properties update as expected.
steps.expectedOutcome: The test suite now includes a test that verifies the component responds correctly to different prop values.
successCriteria: A new test case is added that uses wrapper.setProps() to pass props and checks the component's state or computed properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a test that verifies component behavior with props. This completes the lesson on test context.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a test, but make sure it uses wrapper.setProps() to pass props and checks the component's response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test for props is missing or incorrect. Add a new it() block that uses wrapper.setProps() and verifies the component's behavior changes.
